rows.label: A Record
rows.value: Maps domain/subdomain to IPv4 address. Starting point — always run IP WHOIS on result. Multiple A records = load balancing or CDN. Wildcard (*.domain.com) = default IP for any undefined subdomain.

rows.label: AAAA Record
rows.value: Maps domain/subdomain to IPv6 address. Same purpose as A record, different format. IPv6 infrastructure is often less monitored and may bypass IPv4-only CDN coverage. Always query both.

rows.label: MX Record
rows.value: Specifies which server(s) receive email. Priority value: lower = higher priority. aspmx.l.google.com = Google Workspace. mail.protection.outlook.com = Microsoft 365. Own server hostname = self-hosted, real IP, no CDN.

rows.label: NS Record
rows.value: Specifies authoritative nameservers for the zone. Reveals DNS hosting provider (Cloudflare, AWS Route 53, self-managed). Self-managed NS = potential zone transfer target. NS accounts = DNS hijacking risk.

rows.label: TXT Record
rows.value: Text data: SPF (email sender policy), DMARC (spoofing protection — check p= value), DKIM, service verification tokens. p=none = spoofable domain. Every token = cloud vendor disclosure.

rows.label: CNAME Record
rows.value: Alias pointing to another domain name. Reveals CDN (Cloudflare), SaaS tools (Salesforce force.com, HubSpot, Atlassian). Dangling CNAME (destination NXDOMAIN) = potential subdomain takeover.

rows.label: PTR Record
rows.value: Reverse DNS: IP address to hostname. Stored at in-addr.arpa. Reveals server purpose from hostname. Used by mail servers for anti-spam validation. Run on any IP you discover.

rows.label: SRV Record
rows.value: Service locator: _service._proto.domain → port and target server. _sip._tcp = VoIP. _autodiscover._tcp = Exchange email. _ldap._tcp = Active Directory/LDAP. Confirms specific communication infrastructure.

rows.label: p=none
rows.value: Monitoring only. Emails failing authentication are delivered anyway. Domain CAN be spoofed in phishing. This is a finding — document it.

rows.label: p=quarantine
rows.value: Failed emails go to spam/junk folder. Spoofing is harder but recipients may still see the email.

rows.label: p=reject
rows.value: Failed emails are rejected and not delivered. Strongest protection. Spoofed emails from this domain will be blocked.

rows.label: Zone Transfer (AXFR)
rows.value: Mechanism for copying complete DNS zone from primary to secondary nameserver. Misconfigured = any IP can request complete zone dump. Command: dig axfr @ns1.target.com target.com. ACTIVE — requires written authorisation.

rows.label: Subdomain Brute Force
rows.value: Systematically query common subdomain names (dev, staging, mail, vpn, api, admin, portal, legacy, test). Tools: amass, subfinder, dnsrecon, gobuster. Can be done passively through public resolvers.

rows.label: Certificate Transparency
rows.value: crt.sh — every SSL certificate ever issued for any subdomain is logged publicly. Best passive subdomain discovery source. No contact with target's systems.

rows.label: Dangling CNAME check
rows.value: Query CNAME for each subdomain → check if destination resolves → if NXDOMAIN, check if destination can be claimed. Potential subdomain takeover.

rows.label: Step 1
rows.value: Query A and AAAA records for main domain → IP WHOIS on results → identify CDN or direct server

rows.label: Step 2
rows.value: Query MX records → identify email provider → if self-hosted, IP WHOIS on mail server IP

rows.label: Step 3
rows.value: Query NS records → identify DNS hosting provider → note for zone transfer attempt

rows.label: Step 4
rows.value: Query TXT records → find DMARC p= value → list all SPF include: entries → document service verification tokens

rows.label: Step 5
rows.value: Subdomain enumeration: crt.sh first (passive) → wordlist queries → check each CNAME destination

rows.label: Step 6
rows.value: A and AAAA records for each discovered subdomain → IP WHOIS → flag any direct IPs (no CDN)

rows.label: Step 7
rows.value: PTR lookups on all discovered IPs → hostname reveals server role

rows.label: Step 8
rows.value: Zone transfer attempt (ACTIVE — authorised engagements only): dig axfr @[NS] [domain]

rows.label: dig (Mac/Linux)
rows.value: dig A target.com | dig MX target.com | dig TXT target.com | dig NS target.com | dig AAAA target.com | dig -x IP (PTR) | dig axfr @ns1 target.com (zone transfer, active)

rows.label: nslookup (Windows)
rows.value: nslookup -type=MX target.com | nslookup -type=TXT target.com | nslookup -type=NS target.com

rows.label: mxtoolbox.com
rows.value: DNS Lookup, MX Lookup, TXT/DMARC Lookup — browser-based, no installation

rows.label: crt.sh
rows.value: Certificate Transparency search — passive subdomain discovery

rows.label: bgp.he.net
rows.value: PTR lookup and ASN discovery
